prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement B021 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific chain is complete and independently replicated for about three decades: human incretin physiology (Holst), proglucagon processing and receptor biology (Drucker), and identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), followed by drugs with demonstrated effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The work is mature, and the central appetite actions add a neuroscience dimension that I weigh as a neurologist only in so far as it supports the physiology argument. Round 1 showed that all six of us hold this configuration, but I do not treat that as evidence; the case stands on the mechanism and the outcome data. The citation names physiology and the active form, and mentions treatment only as a consequence, so it does not claim the drug engineering as a prize-worthy discovery.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and round 1 did not resolve it. Habener, who is not on the credited list, has a claim to the identification of the active peptide, and the supplied material does not let us adjudicate it. The three-person limit also leaves out Knudsen, whose acylated analogues made the drugs practical, and a citation that mentions treatment may be read as implying credit to developers who are not laureates. I would not defend Mojsov's seat on the committee's recollection of the history. If the record we can document does not support her identification role, the fallback is a narrower Drucker and Holst pairing, or a different achievement such as B022, and not a trio assembled to fill three seats.

responses.point: Sandberg holds the Drucker, Holst, Mojsov trio, argues that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a discovery in the prize's sense while Knudsen's acylated analogues are closer to engineering of an established mechanism, and names B022 as the cleaner two-person fallback.
responses.response: I accept your discovery-versus-development argument for leaving out Knudsen and it has moved me from uncertainty to a settled view on that point: the mechanism was established before the analogues, and the citation can honour the physiology without pretending to cover pharmaceutical design. Where I stay more cautious is your confidence that the limits can simply be stated openly. If Habener's claim to the identification is serious, openly stating it does not make Mojsov's seat defensible. I agree with you that B022 is the right fallback and not B052, since the CAR-T attribution depends on Eshhar and on the role of Rosenberg, neither of which any of us has checked.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked B045 eighth because the credited names (Druker, Lydon, Sawyers) are mostly translational and the BCR-ABL genetics lie outside them, and would put B022 and B012 ahead of B052 as alternatives.
responses.response: Your attribution objection to B045 is fair and I have weighed it. Imatinib is fully mature and the paradigm of targeted therapy, but a citation would have to word the BCR-ABL genetics (Rowley, Nowell and Hungerford, and the early oncogene work) around the three credited people, and that is harder than for B021. I keep B045 only as a second alternative, behind B022, for clinical consequence, not as a competitor to B021. On B012 I agree it is mature and arguably overdue, but I still place it below B045 and B022 because the anti-TNF story rests on a clinical translation by two people, with the cytokine biology credited to others outside the list; I would not oppose it later.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would turn to B022 or B001 if the priority record for the active GLP-1 peptide cannot be settled, and asks whether cGAS-STING or the unfolded protein response is the lead alternative.
responses.response: I agree that if the B021 attribution fails, the fallback should be chosen on attribution quality and not on clinical reach, and on that criterion B022 is ahead of B001: Mori and Walter are a clean pair with three decades of confirmation, while cGAS-STING has five credited names to split between Chen, Barber, Ishikawa, Sun and Wu and no established therapy. I do not think either should displace B021 while the Habener question is open, because open is not the same as unanswerable. Our supplied record and the committee's own checks should decide Mojsov's seat, not the fact that her name has become standard in the narrative.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that crediting only the physiology could be read as ignoring the decisive drug-development step, while including Knudsen displaces a basic discoverer, and notes that a commercially visible success may bias the committee.
responses.response: The bias point is well taken and I have tried to test it: if GLP-1 had no approved drugs, would the physiology alone justify the prize? I think yes, since proglucagon processing, the active peptide and the receptor biology were established as discoveries in their own right. That is why I keep the citation on physiology and give treatment as the consequence. I do not agree that excluding Knudsen displaces the step that reached patients in a way that makes the prize unfair, because the three credited people are the discoverers of the mechanism that those analogues act on; but I accept that this is a judgment of emphasis, and it would change if the committee weighted development more heavily.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification credit can be sustained against Habener's claim from the supplied evidence; this is the one point that could change my configuration.
Whether leaving out Knudsen is acceptable, or whether the committee wants development credited at the expense of a basic discoverer.
The credit histories for CAR-T (Eshhar), imatinib (Rowley, Zimmermann) and SMN2 antisense (Melki, Lefebvre, Singh) rely on recollection and were not checked against the supplied record.
A two-part prize with B022 does not fit the three-person limit with the current credited sets, so I treat B022 only as a fallback and not as a second part.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted ballot. I worked with Paul Greengard as a postdoctoral fellow and have co-authored with Thomas Perlmann; neither relationship bears on a shortlisted candidate, and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation alone is not a conflict, so no recusal is indicated.
